messages:
jess: Quick Q — we're updating the rerank endpoint and need guidance on deterministic tie-breaking and backcompat. If score is null or multiple items have equal scores, what's the recommended fallback? Trying to finalise SDK behavior and canary plan.

sam: Today we do `sort by score desc`, then fall back to whatever the sort implementation returns if equal. Not deterministic across languages/clients. We should standardize.

neil: Suggestion: server-side deterministic fallback. Compute a `tie_hash` = sha256(request_id || '::' || item.id) and sort by (score desc, tie_hash asc). Include `tie_hash` in `rank_meta` if client asks for it. That keeps it reproducible and requires no client changes for correctness.

anya: Two quick concerns: (1) leaking `request_id` in a response-derived value may correlate requests across items — privacy angle. (2) Some clients rely on original input order for stable UX — will this change observable ordering?

sam: Good points. For (1) we can derive seed from model_version + shortened request_nonce (HMAC) so it's not raw request_id. For (2) we'll add an opt-in flag `stable_tiebreak` in request params (default: false) so existing clients keep current behavior unless opt in.

jess: That sounds reasonable. For backcompat: `rank_meta` should be optional and absent by default. New SDKs can opt in to `stable_tiebreak=true` and read `rank_meta.tie_hash` if present. Older clients get previous behavior unchanged.

neil: Draft spec snippet (server).

```json
{
  "request": {
    "query": "what's the best redwood plan?",
    "items": [ {"id": "item_123", "payload": {...}}, {"id": "item_456"} ],
    "params": { "top_k": 5, "stable_tiebreak": true }
  }
}
```

And a sample response (partial):

```json
{
  "results": [
    {"id": "item_456", "score": 0.82, "rank_meta": {"tie_hash": "0f3a..."}},
    {"id": "item_123", "score": 0.82, "rank_meta": {"tie_hash": "1b8c..."}},
    {"id": "item_789", "score": null }
  ]
}
```

sam: Implementation notes: - default behaviour unchanged when `stable_tiebreak` omitted or false - `tie_hash` only returned when `rank_meta` requested to avoid payload bloat - tie resolution order = score (desc), tie_hash (asc). Document the exact algorithm and hex format.

anya: For privacy, prefer HMAC(seed=service_key, msg=request_id||item.id) and only include first 16 hex chars of the digest in `tie_hash`. That avoids exposing raw identifiers.

neil: Agreed. Also add a feature flag and rollout to Dedicated and Hosted separately. We'll enable in staging, run cross-language client integration tests.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/742 — includes spec docs, unit tests, and telemetry. CI: all tests passing :white_check_mark:.

sam: I'll own server changes and integration tests. @neil can you add SDK shim and doc updates?

neil: Yep — will add to the JS/Go/Java shims and a migration note in the SDK changelog.

jess: Perfect. Can we have a short RFC doc by EOD Thursday? Need it for the canary plan.

sam: Will draft and ping for reviews. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
